lens: Solid-mechanics theory: S as the discrete Steklov–Poincaré (Dirichlet-to-Neumann) map of a thin, doubly-curved shell (the P-sheet, t ≈ 2–2.5 background elements) cut unfitted from a fixed grid; its properties derived from the variational (minimum-energy) definition, its spectrum from shell theory (membrane ∝ t vs bending ∝ t³), its geometry dependence from shape-derivative and active-set arguments, and its assembly behaviour from Loewner-order composition.
principles: P1 (variational identity). g^T S g = 2 × min strain(+GP) energy of the cell with trace g. Symmetry, PSD, exact 6-dim rigid null space, S ≤ K_ΓΓ, S ≤ any Galerkin-coarser model, and Loewner monotonicity (K1 ≤ K2 ⇒ S1 ≤ S2) all follow; thicker, more GP, and even active-set activation are PSD additions, so S is monotone in τ ACROSS switches (the 59.8% event was a monotone jump; cross-seat spectra are one-sided, mu_min ≈ 0.995).

P2 (energy-norm certificate). eps_op ≤ ε ⇔ (1−ε)A ≤ Â ≤ (1+ε)A ⇔ every trace displacement's energy reproduced to ±ε. Basis-, unit-, frame-invariant, and the only module statement preserved by assembly (sums and congruences keep Loewner order).

P3 (thin-plate spectrum). cond(A) ≈ (L/2h_node) × 12(L/t)² ≈ 32 × (2–3)e3 = 6e4–1e5 for t ≈ 0.06–0.08, bracketing the measured 7.2e4 [METRIC]. The floor λ_min ≈ 5e-7 and the 188 sub-1e-6 modes [STRUCTURE OF S] are shell bending (near-inextensional) physics; no stabilisation choice changes them.

P4 (cancellation). Soft-mode stiffness = g^T K_ΓΓ g − g^T C g with the two terms ~E h per node and their difference ~D k³: ratio 1 (mesh-scale) to 1e3–1e4 (bending) [STRUCTURE OF S]. Bending stiffness is non-local; Frobenius-dominant near field is the least important part in the energy metric; per-entry precision on a factor must be eps/√cond ≈ 1e-4 [ACCURACY REQUIREMENTS], and this is physics (t, h), not an artefact.

P5 (far field is Saint-Venant). Interior elliptic regularity ⇒ smooth Green's kernel between separated boundary clusters ⇒ rank ~ (log 1/tol)²; mechanically only 6 resultants + a few warping modes survive beyond one decay length (~0.15–0.25 cell for a strip of width 0.5–0.7): the measured '8 singular values ≥ 99.5%' is '6 + 2'. Near field = discretised differential/hypersingular operator + cut-cell detail: full rank, incompressible by smoothness.

P6 (two stiffness families, two thickness laws). Membrane modes scale as t, bending modes as t³; a uniform τ scaling by (1+δ) multiplies the two ends of the spectrum by (1+δ) and (1+δ)³. Directions outside that window are stabilisation-dominated by elimination — a cheap, physically justified classifier of directions.

P7 (switching). With a hard active-set rule, S(θ) is piecewise real-analytic with Loewner-monotone jumps spaced ~1e-4 in relative τ (level-set surface moves ~1e-4 h per 1e-4 τ across ~5e3 cut cells). Each jump adds ~γEh ≈ 3e-6 of stabiliser: O(1) in the whitened metric on directions at the ~1e-6 floor, O(1e-3) on physical directions — hence 59.8% on a 1.1e-6 direction, 87% derivative disagreement for the operator, 0.023% agreement for end-load compliance [GEOMETRY SENSITIVITY]. Not thin-connection physics: a t³ hinge would need a bridge responding 2000× faster than τ, and sub-h/10 bridges are represented only as (volume fraction)×E + GP.

P8 (what neighbours can feel). In a lattice, fragment/sliver directions are held by the neighbour's connected sheet (the level-set band is continuous across interfaces) and change the assembled response by ≲ λ_frag/λ_phys ≈ 1e-3; the coherent bending family is exactly what lattice-scale bending/shear is built from and must be certified at full weight. A stiffness cut cannot separate the two (both at ~1e-6); mode shape can.

P9 (amplification ladder). Parameter error → eps_op: operator entries ×cond = 7.2e4 (5.5e-5/entry measured); factor entries ×√cond ≈ 111–269 (1.2–2.7e-4/entry); subdomain DtN of size ℓ ×√cond_ℓ ≈ 45 (ℓ=1/2), 11 (1/4), 3 (1/8); multiplicatively-parametrised material/thickness fields in a physical coarse model ×1 exactly (elementwise (1±δ)C ⇒ (1±δ)S). Learn local, condense exactly.

P10 (the 1.111 obstacle is kinematic). Slaving the collar's inner boundary to coarse Q1 kinematics is a subspace constraint (Loewner stiffening) that no core material can undo; the fix is kinematics (deeper collar, shell/enriched core, richer transition), testable with the existing oracle before any learning.

P11 (label hygiene). A physically justified label is consistent, Loewner-monotone in τ, C¹ in (τ,a,b) at fixed grid, cube-equivariant, and has no direction whose stiffness is set by γ rather than by material: AgFEM-type extension with a smooth (not classified) blend, islands deleted, ghost weights scaled by a C¹ ramp of support measure. It leaves the bending floor and the 1e-4 requirement untouched.
implications_for_representation: Mechanics ranks the candidate objects by how much a parameter error is amplified into the whitened worst-direction error (P9). Direct operator entries (×7.2e4 worst case) and factor entries (×111–269) both require the network to reproduce a near/far cancellation of 1e3–1e4 to 1e-4 relative per number; this requirement is set by t and h through cond(A) and cannot be engineered away by stabilisation (P3, P4). Boundary-integral representations of a thin body have the same cancellation between the two sheet faces (thin-body BEM ill-conditioning) and are contraindicated; shell theory is the analytic resolution of that cancellation (t³/12 from through-thickness integration), which says the cancellation should be resolved analytically or by exact elimination, not by regression. The hierarchical/H format is the right deterministic FORMAT for a produced S (gauge-free when built from a given operator; 13.9–15.6% of dense at ±3% [REPRESENTATIONS TRIED]) and for cell actions in a lattice solver, but a poor learning target: fixed-basis far blocks need 1e-4–1e-5 coefficient accuracy, SVD bases are gauge-ambiguous, coefficients are not continuous labels. The representation mechanics itself suggests is a reduced physical model per cell with exact condensation: a fine cut-cell collar (exact trace kinematics, exact null space, exact mesh-scale modes) plus a coarse core with shell-adequate kinematics (Reissner–Mindlin on φ=0 with nominal fields E t, E t³/12(1−ν²), κGt from t = 2τ/|∇φ|, joined to the collar through Kirchhoff kinematics; or an enriched Q2/EAS solid core), with learned MULTIPLICATIVE corrections to the nominal fields. Then symmetry, PSD, rigid null space, cube equivariance, Loewner monotonicity in the fields, continuity in geometry, and the cancellation are all exact by construction, and the certificate is inherited without amplification: field corrections within (1±δ) ⇒ Ŝ within (1±δ) of the nominal model's S. The residual is the model floor (oracle-computable per geometry; 1.111 for fixed one-layer collar + Q1 core, for kinematic reasons, P10). Expected inference cost once cut-cell assembly is compiled: ~50k reduced dofs, ~1–3 s per cell for the full trace condensation; for a lattice, do not condense at all — assemble reduced cells and solve iteratively, using the fine trace only for certification and for mixed-fidelity assembly with teacher cells at load introduction. If a direct-operator route is nevertheless pursued, the only mechanics-compatible form is a factor (multiplicative error, no cond amplification) with a fixed, geometry-computable spatial hierarchy (bisection on the fixed grid, masked), with the dof-compliance column scale computed from local geometry (R² 0.98 [REPRESENTATIONS TRIED]), and with block products/actions supervised instead of coefficients.
implications_for_loss_and_metric: The certificate must remain a worst-direction Loewner statement (P2): the assembly theorem (1−ε)S_c ≤ Ŝ_c ≤ (1+ε)S_c ∀c ⇒ (1−ε)K ≤ K̂ ≤ (1+ε)K gives compliance within ε/(1∓ε), energy-norm displacement within ε/(1−ε), for every lattice, load and boundary condition, and it is tight (a neighbour is an arbitrary load). Averaged losses (D/d, Frobenius, action-MSE) are max-norm blind by 100× [METRIC] because energy norms are suprema over loads; three fragment-type modes can and did decide a verdict. Physically legitimate relaxations, in order of scope: (II) neighbour-aware module certificate |g^T(Ŝ−S)g| ≤ ε g^T(S + S_env)g, computable by whitening with the factor of A + A_env (A_env = Schur complement of a reference neighbourhood onto the cell's trace; the 2-cell harness gives the face version), composable to |δK| ≤ 2εK on interior interfaces, down-weighting exactly the fragment directions that no assembly can exploit while leaving bending directions at full weight (S_env ≈ S there); (III) relative-plus-consistent |g^T(Ŝ−S)g| ≤ ε g^T S g + τ_s g^T J g with J the ghost-jump seminorm, τ_s at the stabilisation scale (whiten with A + (τ_s/ε)J), legitimate because the assembled error is then a GP-class consistent perturbation already covered by the Tet10 validation; (IV) registered task-level certificates only with fixed lattice family, BCs, loads, design region AND sensitivities, plus teacher checkpoints along the TO path because the optimizer is adversarial; (V) mode B needs only spectral bounds (PCG iterations ~√(μ_max/μ_min)) but presupposes a cheap fine action. No Loewner bound controls dŜ/dθ; consistency of the surrogate's own AD gradient suffices for descent, and correctness of the optimum requires the surrogate's error to vary slowly in θ — automatic for a smooth-field surrogate with a smooth model floor, not for a per-entry regressor. Training loss: with a field parametrisation the amplification is ≤1, so a two-sided extreme-eigenvalue loss (Lanczos on the whitened operator, k ≈ 32 at each end, since a one-sided extreme-mode term fixed μ_max and hurt μ_min [LEARNING ATTEMPTS]) plus a bulk term is well conditioned; the gradient of a mode's μ w.r.t. a local field is that mode's strain-energy density there (shape-derivative structure), i.e. interpretable and well scaled. Field labels are non-unique (several internal configurations give near-identical boundary responses), so define per-seat oracle fields as the nearest-to-analytic-baseline optimum to make them unique and continuous in geometry. Use the thickness-exponent test (P6) between τ-scaled seats to classify directions as membrane/bending/stabilisation before deciding what a metric should weight.
implications_for_data_and_teacher: Labels: with the hard active-set GP, S(θ) is piecewise real-analytic with Loewner-monotone jumps spaced ~1e-4 in relative τ; the jumps are ~3e-6 absolute and O(1) whitened on stabilisation-dominated directions (P7). A continuous network can fit the smooth part only, so against current labels the training signal on the deciding directions is unlearnable noise. Recommendation on open decision (4): regenerate with a continuous stabilisation — AgFEM-type extension of weak cells to strong roots with a C¹ blend weight w(v) on the support measure instead of a classifier (the 1e-12 flip → 1.25 [GEOMETRY SENSITIVITY] is the classifier), ghost weights scaled by w(v_min), island components with no path to the trace deleted (they carry no load and are pure stabiliser), all PSD additions so monotonicity is kept; validate as before (Tet10 compliance 0.05–0.10%, γ-halving sensitivity 0.007–0.04%) and add the derivative test (central differences at h = 1e-4 vs 1e-3 must agree to O(h²) in the whitened metric). Cost ≈ 1024 × 31.85 s on 64 cores ≈ 9 h [GOAL]. It will not lower the bending floor or the 1e-4 per-entry requirement; it removes the ~6 fragment modes and the O(1) sensitivities. Data: the 1024 condensed packets can be given factors by dense Cholesky of A (12.8k, ~7e11 flops, seconds) — data volume is not the bottleneck; coverage is (8 τ + 4 plane parameters, 33–1024 samples), and cross-seat whitened distances of 536–7298 [GEOMETRY SENSITIVITY, LIPSCHITZ.json] are dominated by directions that are slivers in the anchor and material in the other seat (one-sided spectra, mu_min ≈ 0.995), so the useful geometric variation is far smaller than that number suggests. A physics-baseline-plus-correction target (nominal shell fields from t = 2τ/|∇φ|) needs orders of magnitude fewer samples than a direct τ→S regressor that must learn the t vs t³ laws from 33 examples. The 48-element cube group gives exact equivariance (build it in via a symmetric coarse mesh or symmetrise at inference), not coverage. Teacher facts to exploit: the sheet thickness is 2τ/|∇φ| (varies √3 across the cell even at uniform τ), the trace is 100% on outer faces with the P-surface meeting faces orthogonally, all labels FULL [GOAL]; cut-plane free edges and the thinnest regions (largest |∇φ|) are where the softest local modes live and where labels should be densest.
implications_for_architecture: Input must be the whole sheet: global bending stiffness depends on thickness everywhere, so a 3D field network on the active band (~23% of 65³ voxels ≈ 63k) with a global receptive field (U-Net/FNO-type) is required; six face images with receptive radius 0.23 cannot represent it, which is what V1's 27% plateau on train and held-out alike shows [LEARNING ATTEMPTS]. Output should be smooth local fields on a fixed coarse structure (per-coarse-element multiplicative corrections to nominal shell/solid tensors, ~1e4–1e5 numbers), never cancelling numbers; the combinatorics that are discontinuous in geometry (active set, trace node set, ghost-face graph, collar cells) are computed exactly from the analytic level set at inference, so the network never has to represent a jump. Rigid invariance, symmetry and PSD must be structural (strain-based elements give them for any tensor); the 38.8% diagonal-only attractor [LEARNING ATTEMPTS] is what a parametrisation without them produces. Parametrise tensors multiplicatively relative to a nominal physical tensor (Cholesky/log-relative), because RMS perturbations of an ill-conditioned tensor are not small Loewner perturbations. Pretrain on the analytic baseline without the teacher (the baseline alone may already sit within 10–30% of the teacher — measure it first with the Loewner oracle), then fine-tune on the whitened extreme-eigenvalue loss with the exact condensation in the loop (each Ŝ action = one sparse coarse solve, a few tens of ms; use the existing 22× sparse gradient and exact-inverse tools). Equivariance: exact via group symmetrisation over the 48 ops or an equivariant backbone. If an H-format is needed at deployment, build it deterministically from the produced Ŝ, not by prediction. Before any training, run the oracle ladder: analytic-shell baseline → collar depth 1/2/3 → core kinematics Q1/Q2/shell, each with its closed-form/optimised field floor, and only start learning on a configuration whose floor is below the gate.
hard_constraints: [METRIC] Acceptance is worst-direction eps_op = max|mu−1| (±10% work, ±3% target); D/d and every averaged loss mislead by ~100× (0.0295 ↔ 58; 1.27e-5 ↔ 0.229; 3 of 12,792 modes decided a verdict).
[METRIC] cond(A) = 7.2e4 (λ 4.9e-7…3.5e-2); additive error is amplified by cond(A) (±3% worst case needs ||E||₂ ≤ 1.46e-8, 4.2e-7 relative); multiplicative factor error is not (eps_op ≈ 1.42||Δ||).

[STRUCTURE OF S] S is not sparse in any useful sense: soft-direction stiffness is a near/far cancellation of ratio 1e3–1e4; banding the true factor to any radius fails (radius 0.25, 6% of entries: eps_op 58; ~300 damaged modes at every radius). 99.87% of off-diagonal Frobenius energy within 0.05 (=1.6h), far face-face blocks: top-8 SVs ≥ 99.5%.

[STRUCTURE OF S] The softest modes are physical: 188 modes < 1e-6 without sliver dominance; ~6 fragment modes; all directions numerically measurable (min E/N = 1.5e27) — nothing may be masked on storage-floor grounds.

[ACCURACY REQUIREMENTS] A direct factor predictor needs ~2.7e-4 per entry (independent) to ~1.2e-4 (coherent); A itself ~5.5e-5; which noise model a real network follows is unknown; a 1e-3 RMS perturbation of the old backend's diagonal parameters moved the spectrum to [0.707, 1.377].

[GEOMETRY SENSITIVITY] +1e-4 τ scaling: ||A||_F changes 2.3e-4 but one 1.1e-6-stiffness direction by 59.8% (activated cell of volume fraction 5.6e-15, 3 new GP faces); operator central differences at h=1e-4 vs 1e-3 disagree by 87%, end-load compliance derivative agrees to 0.023%; the internal-extension prototype gives 1.016 but flips to 1.25 on a 1e-12 threshold change; production labels use the original GP.

[GEOMETRY SENSITIVITY] Cross-seat eps_op 536–3847 (up to 7298 in the raw data) at τ-distance 0.14–0.36, one-sided (mu_min ≈ 0.995): no zero-shot transplant; 33 factored seats sparsely sample an 8+4-parameter geometry space.

[ASSEMBLY] Exact condensation composes to 1e-12; teacher validated against body-fitted Tet10 at 0.05–0.10% compliance; 2-cell: eps_op 0.152 → displacement 4.1%, compliance ≤ 0.31%; 0.026 → 0.94%; displacement ≈ eps_op/4; compliance is first order in general and its smallness here is construction-specific and not transferable; sensitivities untested; deployment mode A vs B undecided.

[REPRESENTATIONS TRIED] Unfitted H-matrix of R* passes ±3% at 13.9–15.6% of dense on 4 seats (adaptive ranks from the true blocks; SVD gauge non-unique; approximating A costs 1.17× more); collar + coarse Q1 core with 6×6 SPD tensors reaches eps_op 0.15 but a Loewner lower bound proves fixed one-layer collar cannot pass ±10% (mu_max ≥ 1.111); its end-to-end cost is ~30 s and still depends on the fine factor; T^T D T and banded-L + low-rank M constructions are 37–600× off the gate.
[REPRESENTATIONS TRIED] The dof compliance (column scale) is predictable from local geometry: R² 0.98 within a cell, leave-one-seat-out median spread 16.8.

[LEARNING ATTEMPTS] Only one geometry→operator generalisation experiment exists (6-face CNN, receptive radius 0.23, banded L + rank-512 M, 26 labels): 27% error on train and held-out alike, mu_max up to 670; Frobenius-loss dense attempts stuck at the 38.8% diagonal-only attractor; a one-sided extreme-mode loss improved mu_max 15→5 and worsened mu_min 0.13→0.05.

[GOAL] Teacher: CutFEM Q2, n=32, GP γ=η=1e-4; seat 0328: 231,192 dofs, trace 12,798 (5.54%), d = q−6 = 12,792 via quotient B; 7,478 active cells, 18,092 GP faces; 31.85 s condensation on 64 cores; all 33 factored labels FULL; 48-element cube group is exact equivariance; the material is |φ| ≤ τ(x) with φ = cos2πx+cos2πy+cos2πz, τ trilinear from 8 corners, plus a half-space cut (repo code), so geometric thickness is 2τ/|∇φ|.
open_questions: Direction classification: run the thickness-exponent test (two seats differing only by a uniform τ scale (1+δ); whitened spectrum should cluster at (1+δ) for membrane and (1+δ)³ for bending; outliers are stabilisation-dominated) and an energy-partition test (membrane vs bending energy of the 188 soft eigenmodes via the level-set normal). How many directions are stabilisation-dominated, and are they exactly the ones that decide eps_op?

Model floor vs kinematics: what is the Loewner lower bound of the collar+core model as a function of collar depth (1, 2, 3 layers) and core kinematics (Q1, Q2/EAS, Reissner–Mindlin shell on φ=0)? Does any configuration have a floor below ±3%, and at what reduced dof count?

Analytic baseline: how far is a NO-LEARNING nominal model (shell fields E t, E t³/12(1−ν²), κGt from t = 2τ/|∇φ|, plus exact collar) from the teacher in eps_op? If it is within 10–30%, the learning problem is a small multiplicative correction.

Label regeneration: does a C¹-blended AgFEM-type stabilisation keep the Tet10 validation (0.05–0.10%), pass the derivative test (h=1e-4 vs 1e-3 agreeing to O(h²) in the whitened metric), and remove the ~6 fragment modes without introducing new near-floor directions? Actual sheet thickness t = 2τ/|∇φ| for the labelled seats should be read off the packets to confirm the t ≈ 0.06–0.08 inference used here.

Environment operator: what is S_env for a bulk cell (Schur complement of a 3×3×3 neighbourhood or a periodic image onto Γ_c), how much does a neighbour-aware certificate (II) relax the module gate on the fragment directions while leaving the bending family unchanged, and how does it behave when the neighbour also has a sliver at the same interface nodes?

Sensitivities: is the surrogate's AD gradient dŜ/dθ consistent with the teacher's stable task-level derivative (0.023% path) on the physical subspace, and how large is the sensitivity error of a smooth surrogate relative to the design changes a TO step makes?

Mode B economics: what does the fine action cost without the full condensation (K_II factorisation alone, or an iterative interior solve preconditioned by the coarse model)? Mode B only makes sense if the fine action is much cheaper than 31.85 s per cell.

Uniqueness and continuity of field labels: with a nearest-to-baseline regularisation, are per-seat oracle fields continuous in geometry across seats (leave-one-seat-out), and is their leave-one-out predictability comparable to the R² 0.98 found for dof compliance?

Lattice deliverable: for TO on N ≈ 10³ cells, is 'assemble reduced cells (~5e4 dofs each) and solve iteratively' acceptable versus explicit per-cell S (1.3 GB dense, ~200 MB H-compressed per cell)? This decides whether condensation is needed at inference at all or only for certification.

Which noise model a real field network follows (coherent multiplicative vs Loewner-relative), and whether the exact ≤1 amplification of multiplicatively-parametrised fields survives a network's systematic bias near cut-plane free edges and the thinnest regions of the sheet.

THE INTERFACE SCHUR COMPLEMENT OF A THIN-SHEET TPMS CELL: WHAT IT IS, WHY IT IS HARD, AND WHAT MECHANICS SAYS A NETWORK SHOULD PRODUCE

Setting and notation. Unit cube cell (side L = 1), background grid n = 32 (element size h = 1/32, Q2 node spacing h_node = 1/64). Material Ω = {x in the cube : |φ(x)| ≤ τ(x), a·x ≤ b}, with φ = cos2πx + cos2πy + cos2πz, τ trilinear in the 8 corner values, and a half-space cut (a, b) (this is how the repository's support-weight code defines the geometry; [GOAL] lists the same parameters). The geometric sheet thickness is t = 2τ/|∇φ|, and on φ = 0 the gradient magnitude runs from 2π to 2π√3, so even a uniform τ gives a sheet whose thickness varies by a factor √3 ≈ 1.7 across the cell; the sheet is thinnest where |∇φ| is largest. I did not have the τ values on this host. From the node counts (4,266 trace nodes over 6 faces, a trace curve of perimeter ≈ 1.53 per face, ≈ 98 node columns along it, ≈ 7.3 across, minus the Q2 support margin) and independently from cond(A) (below), t ≈ 0.06–0.08 for seat 0328, i.e. 2–2.5 background elements; the active-cell count (7,478 = 22.8% of the grid, against a P-surface area of ≈ 2.35 per cell) gives a cut band ≈ 0.097 wide ≈ 3 elements, consistent with t plus partial cells. Everything below that depends on t uses this inference and should be checked against 2τ/|∇φ| read from the packets.

K = K_body + γ K_ghost with γ = 1e-4 [GOAL]; each ghost face is a dense 135-dof block over the 45 nodes of its two cells (repository), i.e. a penalty on the disagreement of the two cells' polynomial extensions. Partition into interior I and trace Γ; S = K_ΓΓ − K_ΓI K_II⁻¹ K_IΓ; A = B S Bᵀ removes the 6 rigid modes, d = 12,792 [GOAL]. Whitened spectrum μ = eig(R*⁻ᵀ Â R*⁻¹), eps_op = max|μ − 1| [METRIC].

1. WHAT S IS

1.1 Definition. S g is the vector of nodal reactions on Γ when the trace is prescribed to g, every other surface of the sheet is traction-free, and the interior is in equilibrium. It is the discrete Steklov–Poincaré (Dirichlet-to-Neumann) map of the cell.

1.2 The variational identity, and everything that follows from it. gᵀ S g = min over u_I of [g; u_I]ᵀ K [g; u_I] = twice the minimal strain-plus-ghost energy compatible with the trace g. All exact properties are corollaries:
(i) symmetry — Betti reciprocity;
(ii) positive semidefiniteness — energy is nonnegative;
(iii) null space = rigid motions restricted to Γ, exactly 6-dimensional iff the discrete body is connected in the graph of K (which, with GP, includes ghost-face couplings). d = q − 6 [GOAL] certifies that the GP teacher's cell is graph-connected. Slivers held only by ghost faces are not null, but they sit at the ghost stiffness scale (Section 3.4). Island components with no path to the trace would be null vectors of K_II and are what GP had to make solvable in the first place (no-GP cond ≈ 4e16 [STRUCTURE OF S]);
(iv) S ≤ K_ΓΓ (a clamped interior is stiffer), and S ≤ S_coarse for any Galerkin model whose interior space is a subspace of the fine one (Rayleigh–Ritz). This is the origin of the Loewner lower bound that excludes the fixed one-layer collar (Section 6.3);
(v) Loewner monotonicity under stiffening: K₁ ≤ K₂ ⇒ S₁ ≤ S₂, because the minimum of a larger quadratic form is larger. Three corollaries matter here. Adding material (larger τ) is a PSD addition ⇒ S increases in every direction. Adding ghost penalty is a PSD addition ⇒ S_GP ≥ S_noGP. And — less obvious — activating a background cell is also monotone: the new cell adds its 81-dof element block and its ghost-face blocks, a PSD form on the enlarged space, and minimising the enlarged energy over the extra interior dofs still bounds below the old minimum. So on the common trace, S is monotone in τ even across active-set switches. The 59.8% incident [GEOMETRY SENSITIVITY] must therefore be a monotone jump (μ_max = 1.598 with μ_min ≥ 1 − O(1e-4)), and the cross-seat spectra in the repository's LIPSCHITZ data have the same one-sided signature (μ_min 0.9947–0.9953, μ_max 537–7298 against anchor 0328). The label's defect is the size of the jump, not its sign;
(vi) the energy-norm certificate: eps_op ≤ ε ⇔ (1−ε)A ≤ Â ≤ (1+ε)A ⇔ the strain energy of every trace displacement is reproduced to ±ε. This is invariant under changes of trace basis, units and frame, and it is the only module statement preserved by assembly (Section 5). Its two-sidedness is physical: a surrogate can be too soft (spurious mechanisms) or too stiff (locked kinematics), and a lattice can exploit either.

1.3 Continuum scaling. In the continuum, S is a pseudodifferential operator of order +1 on Γ (H^{1/2} → H^{−1/2}). For a bulk body its symbol grows like μ|k| in the surface wavenumber; the discrete top is set by the first element layer, λ_max ≈ E h: measured 3.5e-2 ≈ 1/32 [METRIC] with E = 1. A thin sheet has two constitutive families instead of one: membrane (stiffness per unit length ~ E t k) and bending (~ D k³, D = E t³/12(1−ν²)). Their ratio at cell scale is t²/12L² ≈ 3e-4 to 5e-4 for t = 0.06–0.08; the mesh-to-cell wavenumber factor is L/(2 h_node) ≈ 32; so cond(A) ≈ 32 × 12(L/t)² ≈ 6e4–1.1e5, bracketing the measured 7.2e4 [METRIC]. The teacher's spectrum is a thin-plate spectrum whose condition number is explained to within a factor 1.5 by t and h alone. This is not a stabilisation artefact and no stabilisation choice will change it: the floor λ_min ≈ 4.9e-7 and the 188 modes below 1e-6 with no sliver dominance [STRUCTURE OF S] are the bending family of a shell two elements thick.

2. NEAR FIELD, FAR FIELD

2.1 Why the far field is low rank. For trace nodes i, j: S_ij = K_ij − (K_iI) K_II⁻¹ (K_Ij). The second term is the interior Green's function sampled at the elements adjacent to i and j. By interior elliptic regularity the Green's function of a constant-coefficient elliptic system is real-analytic away from the diagonal, so on a pair of boundary clusters (σ, τ) with dist ≥ c·diam it has a degenerate expansion whose rank grows only like (log 1/tol)² for surface clusters — the H-matrix/FMM admissibility condition. Saint-Venant is the mechanics reading: only the resultants (6 per patch) and a few low-order warping/stretching modes propagate beyond one decay length; for a plate strip of width w the self-equilibrated remainder decays like exp(−c x/w) with c between π and 4.2 (Papkovich–Fadle), i.e. a decay length ≈ 0.15–0.25 cell for the sheet's local width 0.5–0.7. Opposite faces (distance 1) exchange essentially resultants only; adjacent faces (centroid distance ≈ 0.7) resultants plus a few modes. The measurement 'top-8 singular values carry ≥ 99.5% of far face-face block energy' [STRUCTURE OF S] is exactly '6 + 2'.

2.2 Why the near field is not. 0.05 is 1.6 h, the footprint of a Q2 element patch. '99.87% of off-diagonal Frobenius energy within centroid distance 0.05' [STRUCTURE OF S] says ‖S‖_F is dominated by K_ΓΓ, the direct element coupling along the strip, with entries ~E h. This is the hypersingular part of the DtN kernel (|x−y|⁻³ on a surface) plus the element stiffness: a discretised differential operator whose local singular values follow the operator symbol at mesh wavenumbers and do not decay until every local dof is included. It also carries the cut-cell detail — support fractions of node bases spanning 1e-4 to 1 (the repository's dof-compliance regression: log w alone gives R² 0.867 of a 7.5e3 compliance spread), 45-node ghost patches — which is not a smooth function of position and is not compressible by smoothness.

2.3 The inversion of importance. Frobenius importance and energy-metric importance are opposite. The soft modes are decided by the small far-field corrections cancelling the large near-field entries (Section 3). Near field: big, dense, incompressible, and the least important part if the far field is wrong. Far field: small, smooth, low-rank, and decisive. Any representation that spends accuracy by entry magnitude — banding, thresholding, Frobenius or action-MSE losses — spends it on the wrong part, which is why the banded true factor at radius 0.25 (6% of entries) still has eps_op = 58 with ~300 damaged modes at every radius and μ_max stuck at 59–144 [STRUCTURE OF S].

3. THE SOFTEST MODES AND THE CANCELLATION

3.1 Mechanism. For a trace field g: gᵀ S g = gᵀ K_ΓΓ g − gᵀ C g, C = K_ΓI K_II⁻¹ K_IΓ. The first term is the energy of g extended by zero into the cell: for a strip displaced by δ normal to the sheet it is ~E h δ² per node (a step across the first element layer). The second is the energy recovered when the interior relaxes: for a smooth bending pattern the sheet follows the strip over a distance 1/k and only ~D k³ per unit length remains. Per mode, the ratio (K_ΓΓ term)/(S term) runs from ~1 for mesh-scale patterns the interior cannot help with, to E h/(bending stiffness per node) ≈ 1e3–1e4 for the bending family — the measured near/far cancellation ratio [STRUCTURE OF S]. Physically: bending stiffness is not a sum of local boundary stiffnesses; it is a property of the whole sheet transmitted through the interior.

3.2 What this costs in precision. For R̂ = (I+Δ)R*, eps_op ≈ 1.42‖Δ‖ [METRIC]. Entry-relative noise ε on R* gives Δ = E R*⁻¹ with ‖Δ‖ ≲ ε √(λ_max/λ_min) = 269ε; random partial cancellation gives the measured 111ε (eps_op 1.11e-2 at ε = 1e-4 [ACCURACY REQUIREMENTS]). So the per-entry precision a factor must carry is eps_gate/√cond(A) ≈ 0.03/269 ≈ 1.1e-4, matching the measured 2.7e-4 (independent) to 1.2e-4 (coherent). That number is set by t and h through cond(A). It is physics, and a better stabilisation will not relax it; it would only remove the ~6 fragment modes and the handful of stabilisation-dominated directions.

3.3 Which trace patterns are soft. Those whose interior extension is nearly inextensional — bending of the mid-surface without stretching. The P-sheet has negative Gaussian curvature everywhere; a doubly curved shell resists transverse deflection partly by membrane action (curvature stiffening), so purely inextensional deformations are constrained (for K < 0 they are governed by a hyperbolic system whose characteristics are the asymptotic curves), and the softest admissible trace patterns are those the interior can accommodate by near-pure bending: in-plane translations of a face's trace ring (an m = 1 pattern of normal-to-sheet displacement), tilts and low harmonics of the six rings combined compatibly. Order-of-magnitude check: displacing one face ring by δ normal to the sheet with the other five held forces curvature ~δ/(0.25)² over ~0.4 of sheet area, gᵀ A g ≈ D × 16 × 0.4 × δ² ≈ 1.7e-4 δ² with D ≈ 2.6e-5 (t ≈ 0.067, ν = 0.3, E = 1); divided by ‖g‖² ≈ 711 δ² (nodes on one strip) this gives λ ≈ 2.4e-7, the scale of λ_min = 4.9e-7 [METRIC]. Higher ring harmonics stiffen like k³, and membrane-coupled patterns (ring breathing, with its edge boundary layer of length √(Rt)) sit near 1e-4. 'Hundreds of modes below 1e-6, not thousands' is what a curved shell predicts; the exact count belongs to the P-surface's inextensional-mode structure and should be read from eigenvectors, not from a plate formula. A direct diagnostic exists with the project's tools: split the strain energy of each of the 188 soft eigenmodes' interior extensions into membrane and bending parts using the level-set normal.

3.4 'Buckling-like' modes and thin connections. Nothing buckles in linear elasticity, but the patterns that would go unstable under compression — short-wavelength transverse deflections where the sheet is locally thinnest (largest |∇φ|), and along the cut plane's free edge, where the bending stiffness of an edge is roughly half that of the interior — are the softest local bending modes. A genuine thin bridge of local thickness t_b is a hinge with stiffness ∝ t_b³, so a relative thickness change δ moves it by 3δ. For δ = 1e-4 to produce 60%, the bridge would have to respond 2000× faster than τ, impossible for a band whose thickness is 2τ/|∇φ| everywhere. Below h/10 the discretisation cannot represent a bridge anyway: it becomes (material volume fraction) × E/h² plus ghost coupling — i.e. at the discrete level 'thin connection physics' and 'sliver activation' are the same object, and that object is not physics.

3.5 Fragment and sliver modes. A piece of the band connected to the main body only through ghost faces (or a sub-element bridge) has six near-rigid modes whose stiffness is set by γ: a ghost face contributes ~γ E h ≈ 1e-4 × 3e-2 = 3e-6 per unit derivative jump — the same decade as the physical bending floor. This coincidence of scales is why a stiffness cut cannot separate the ~6 fragment modes from the 188 bending modes [STRUCTURE OF S]; only mode shape can (spatial coherence, membrane/bending split, smoothness). The no-GP teacher's cond ≈ 4e16 [STRUCTURE OF S] shows what these directions are without stabilisation: essentially zero. They are the stabiliser, not the structure. The storage-floor result (every direction measurable, min E/N = 1.5e27 [STRUCTURE OF S]) says they are numerically well defined; it does not make them physical.

4. HOW GEOMETRY ENTERS

4.1 The smooth part. Within a fixed active set, element matrices are integrals of polynomials over cut sub-cells whose shapes depend smoothly on (τ, a, b); K is real-analytic there, K_II is uniformly SPD (that is what GP buys), so S is real-analytic on each piece. The continuum shape derivative is explicit: for a normal velocity V_n of the sheet's free surfaces, d(gᵀ S g) = ∫ V_n W(u_g) dA over the moving surface, where W(u_g) is the strain-energy density of g's interior extension — PSD for V_n ≥ 0 (monotonicity again) and it says which geometry moves which mode: a thickness change at x moves each mode in proportion to the energy density that mode stores at x. Membrane energy density scales like t and bending like t³, so uniform scaling τ → (1+δ)τ multiplies the stiff end by (1+δ) and the soft end by (1+δ)³; the whitened spectrum between two such seats must cluster at 1+δ and 1+3δ. Consistency check on the incident: +1e-4 in τ moved ‖A‖_F by 2.3e-4 [GEOMETRY SENSITIVITY], inside the (1..3) × 1e-4 window — that part is physics. This 'thickness-exponent test' is cheap and decisive: directions with μ outside [(1+δ), (1+δ)³] beyond discretisation scatter are, by elimination, stabilisation-dominated.

4.2 Switching. On a countable set of hypersurfaces in geometry space the discrete geometry changes: the band |φ| ≤ τ crosses a grid vertex or element edge (new active cell, new nodes and ghost faces, possibly new trace nodes — q varies between seats, d = 12,792 to 15,702 [REPRESENTATIONS TRIED]), the sub-cell cut topology changes (quadrature pattern), or a support measure crosses a threshold. Density: a relative change δ of τ moves the sheet surfaces by ≈ δ t/2 ≈ 3.5e-6 cell = 1e-4 h at δ = 1e-4; with ~5,000 cut cells the expected number of activation events per 1e-4 of τ is of order 1–3, so switching manifolds are spaced ~1e-4 apart and the inter-seat distances 0.14–0.36 [GEOMETRY SENSITIVITY] contain thousands. Each event adds a cell of volume fraction v (physical stiffness ∝ v, negligible: 5.6e-15 in the incident) plus 1–3 ghost faces at ~3e-6 each, acting as a bridge that penalises disagreement between the polynomial extensions of previously weakly coupled neighbouring cells. On a direction of stiffness λ the relative effect is ≈ 3e-6 × (mode's jump content)/λ: O(1) at λ ~ 1e-6, O(1e-3) at λ ~ 3e-3. That is the whole story of 59.8% on a 1.1e-6 direction: a stabilisation-dominated direction received one more stabilisation term. The 87% disagreement of central differences at h = 1e-4 vs 1e-3 is what any function with a jump inside the stencil gives; the 0.023% agreement of the 6-D end-load compliance derivative [GEOMETRY SENSITIVITY] is what the same function gives when projected on directions of stiffness ~1e-3, where the jump is ~1e-3 × alignment. The two facts are consistent and together they locate the jumps in a subspace that end loads barely touch.

4.3 Classification. For the current teacher, S(θ) at fixed grid is piecewise real-analytic; the jumps are dense (spacing ~1e-4 in relative τ), Loewner-monotone, tiny in operator norm (~3e-6 absolute), and O(1) in the whitened metric on the stabilisation-dominated subspace. On the physical subspace — membrane and bending, all the way down to the true floor — S is continuous with bounded whitened derivative (≈ 1–3 per unit relative τ). A continuous network can represent the first part and cannot represent the second; against the current labels the unlearnable part is O(1) on a few dozen directions, which is exactly the number of directions that decide eps_op ('3 modes out of 12,792' [METRIC]).

4.4 A physically justified label. Properties it should have: (a) consistency — converges to the continuum DtN (validated so far only at compliance level, 0.05–0.10% vs Tet10 [ASSEMBLY]); (b) Loewner monotone in τ (already true, Section 1.2); (c) continuous, preferably C¹, in (τ, a, b) at fixed grid; (d) exactly equivariant under the 48 cube operations (already true); (e) no direction whose stiffness is set by γ rather than by material, or, where unavoidable, bounded rather than O(1) whitened sensitivity. Construction: keep the trace and the GP for well-supported cells; for cells with small material support measure v use AgFEM-type extension (Badia–Neiva–Verdugo) — slave the weak dofs to a strong root's polynomial — but replace the classifier by a smooth blend, penalty weight β(v) = β₀(1 − w(v)) with w a C¹ ramp on [0, v₀], so a cell enters the model continuously; delete island components with no path to the trace (they carry no load and are pure stabiliser); scale each ghost face's γ by w(v_min) of its two cells. Every term is PSD, so monotonicity is preserved; the blend is C¹, so S is C¹ in geometry with derivative bounded by β₀/v₀ × (jump energy); and because a slaved dof inherits its root's physical stiffness, blended directions no longer sit at the 1e-6 floor, so their whitened sensitivity is ~1e-3–1e-4 per 1e-4 of τ instead of O(1). The prototype 'internal extension' reached 1.016 and then jumped to 1.25 on a 1e-12 threshold change [GEOMETRY SENSITIVITY] precisely because its classifier was hard; the blend removes the flip. Regeneration cost ≈ 1024 × 31.85 s on 64 cores ≈ 9 h [GOAL]. What it does not do: it does not lower the bending floor (λ_min stays ~5e-7, cond ~7e4, the 1e-4 per-entry requirement stays), and it changes physical modes by a consistent O(γ) amount, so the Tet10 validation must be re-run but should pass unchanged (halving or doubling γ moved compliance by 0.007–0.04% in the existing validation). Acceptance test for the new label: central differences at h = 1e-4 and 1e-3 agree to O(h²) in the whitened metric along the τ path.

5. WHAT A LATTICE NEEDS FROM EACH CELL

5.1 The sandwich theorem. K_lattice = Σ_c P_cᵀ S_c P_c (exact to 1e-12 [ASSEMBLY]). If (1−ε)S_c ≤ Ŝ_c ≤ (1+ε)S_c for every c then (1−ε)K ≤ K̂ ≤ (1+ε)K, because sums and congruences preserve Loewner order. Hence for every load f and every boundary condition: C/(1+ε) ≤ Ĉ ≤ C/(1−ε) (compliance), ‖û − u‖_K ≤ ε/(1−ε) ‖u‖_K (energy-norm displacement), eigenfrequencies within (1±ε)^{1/2}. No lattice topology, load or design enters. Tightness: for any direction g in which Ŝ_c is off by ε_g there is a two-cell configuration and a self-equilibrated interface load whose compliance error is ≈ ε_g — the neighbour is an arbitrary load. So the worst direction is necessary, not merely sufficient, for a universal certificate. Measured: eps_op 0.152 → displacement 4.1%, 0.026 → 0.94% [ASSEMBLY], both inside the bound; compliance ≤ 0.31% because the four end loads are weakly aligned with that construction's error directions — a fact about that construction, not a law [ASSEMBLY].

5.2 Which modes are excited by whom. A bulk cell (all six faces shared) sees the trace displacement that equilibrium with its neighbours imposes. Away from load introduction and lattice boundaries this is smooth at the scale of the geometry variation: low ring harmonics, the coherent bending family, plus Saint-Venant remainders that decay within ~0.2 cell of any load, boundary or geometric contrast between neighbours. The bending family is not 'rarely excited': lattice-scale bending and shear of a sheet lattice are built from it, coherently across cells, so an ε error there is an ε error in the lattice's bending compliance — a compliance-minimising optimizer avoids bending, but a Loewner certificate is objective-agnostic and the optimizer is adversarial. Mesh-scale trace modes (pinching across the strip, alternating patterns) are injected only by loads or geometric discontinuities; in the bulk the neighbour holds them at ~E h. Fragment and sliver directions are held by the neighbour's connected sheet — the level-set band is continuous across the interface, so where this cell is fragmented the neighbour is generally connected — and an error there changes the assembled response by ≲ λ_frag/λ_phys ≈ 1e-3 × alignment: never load-bearing. This is why three fragment-type modes can fail a module while the assembly is fine, and why one cannot infer the converse for the 188 bending modes.

5.3 Why averaged metrics fail, mechanically. D/d sums (μ − log μ − 1): three modes at μ = 1.23 contribute 3 × 0.023/12,792 ≈ 5e-6, invisible, while an assembly can put all of its load into those three directions. Energy norms are suprema over loads; the 100× discrepancy [METRIC] is not a numerical accident.

5.4 Legitimate certificates, ranked by scope.
(I) Universal: full-trace Loewner ±ε — what the project uses. Its cost is that it certifies stabilisation-dominated directions no assembly can exploit.
(II) Neighbour-aware module certificate: |gᵀ(Ŝ_c − S_c)g| ≤ ε gᵀ(S_c + S_env,c) g for all g, where S_env,c is the stiffness the environment presents at Γ_c (Schur complement of a reference neighbourhood onto Γ_c; the 2-cell harness computes the face version). It composes: for bulk cells with all faces shared, summing gives |δK| ≤ 2εK on interior interfaces; lattice-boundary faces need (I) or the teacher. It is computable with the existing evaluator by whitening with the factor of A + A_env instead of R*. It down-weights exactly the fragment directions, by the physics that makes them harmless, and leaves bending directions at essentially full weight (S_env ≈ S there).
(III) Relative-plus-consistent: |gᵀ(Ŝ − S)g| ≤ ε gᵀ S g + τ_s gᵀ J g with J the ghost-jump seminorm (vanishes on smooth fields) and τ_s at the stabilisation scale; whiten with A + (τ_s/ε)J. Legitimate because the assembled error is then a consistent perturbation of the same class as GP itself, already covered by the Tet10 validation.
(IV) Registered task-level: a fixed lattice family, boundary conditions, load set, design region and sensitivities, validated with margin, plus teacher checkpoints along the TO path (every k-th iteration and the final design, 32 s per cell per check) because the optimizer will find any spurious stiffness. Not transferable across constructions [ASSEMBLY].
(V) Mode B: spectral bounds [μ_min, μ_max] set PCG iteration counts (~√(μ_max/μ_min) per decade); still worst-direction, 30× looser, but it presupposes a cheap fine action — which is the elimination being avoided.
Sensitivities: none of (I)–(III) bounds dŜ/dθ; a surrogate can be within ε and have any derivative. Consistency of the surrogate's own AD gradient is enough for the optimizer to descend the surrogate's landscape; correctness of the optimum requires the surrogate's error to vary slowly with θ — automatic for a smooth-field surrogate whose error is a smooth model floor, not for a per-entry regressor whose error field is whatever the network happens to do. The teacher's task-level derivative is stable (0.023%) precisely because the physical shape derivative is; a physically parametrised surrogate inherits that structure.

6. WHICH REPRESENTATION MECHANICS SUGGESTS

6.1 The amplification ladder (parameter error → eps_op).
— Direct operator entries: ×cond(A) = 7.2e4 worst case; 5.5e-5 per entry measured [METRIC, ACCURACY REQUIREMENTS].
— Factor entries: ×√cond ≈ 269 worst case, 111 measured; 1.2–2.7e-4 per entry [ACCURACY REQUIREMENTS].
— Subdomain DtN maps of size ℓ (the fronts of a nested-dissection tree): ×√cond_ℓ with cond_ℓ ≈ (ℓ/2h_node) × 12(ℓ/t)², i.e. ≈ 45 at ℓ = 1/2, 11 at 1/4, 3 at 1/8; the requirement relaxes like ℓ^{3/2}, and at ℓ ≈ 2h the object is the element matrix, which is known exactly from the analytic geometry.
— Material/thickness fields in a physical coarse model: exactly ×1. If (1−δ)C_e ≤ Ĉ_e ≤ (1+δ)C_e for every element tensor then (1−δ)K_model ≤ K̂ ≤ (1+δ)K_model (element stiffness is linear and monotone in C), hence (1−δ)S_model ≤ Ŝ ≤ (1+δ)S_model (Schur monotonicity). A 3% gate is a 3% field accuracy — provided the fields are parametrised multiplicatively relative to a nominal physical tensor (Cholesky- or log-relative), because an RMS perturbation of an ill-conditioned tensor's entries is not a small Loewner perturbation. The observation that a 1e-3 RMS perturbation moved a spectrum to [0.707, 1.377] [ACCURACY REQUIREMENTS] concerned diagonal parameters of a factor-type backend, where amplification is 100–1000; it does not apply to material fields.
The ladder's message: the emergent quantity — bending stiffness produced by a 1e3–1e4 near/far cancellation — should be computed by exact elimination in FP64, not regressed. Learn what is local; condense what is not.

6.2 Boundary-integral and H-structure. A boundary-integral representation of a thin body carries unknowns on both sheet faces a distance t apart, and their kernels nearly cancel: thin-body BEM is ill-conditioned for the same reason S is. Shell theory is the analytic resolution of that cancellation (through-thickness integration of linear strain gives t³/12); the cancellation should be resolved analytically or by exact linear algebra, not statistically. H-structure is the right deterministic FORMAT for a produced S (gauge-free when built from a given operator; 13.9–15.6% of dense at ±3% [REPRESENTATIONS TRIED]) and for cell actions in a lattice solver, but a poor learning target: with fixed geometry-computable bases (rigid + polynomial Saint-Venant modes per cluster) the far-block coefficients must be accurate to 1e-4–1e-5 relative to preserve the cancellation, and a Taylor/Chebyshev rank at admissibility ratio 1/2 and tolerance 1e-4 is ~50–200 per block — consistent with 15% of dense — while SVD bases are gauge-ambiguous and their coefficients are not continuous labels.

6.3 Coarse physical model plus exact condensation: what mechanics predicts and what the 1.111 bound means. The collar + Q1 core [REPRESENTATIONS TRIED (e)] failed for an identifiable reason. The collar's inner boundary is slaved to the coarse core's kinematics; that is a subspace constraint and therefore a Loewner stiffening independent of the core's material — with zero core material the model is the collar with a Q1-constrained inner boundary, and the minimum over all SPD core tensors is bounded below by that. In a sheet two elements thick, the through-thickness bending kinematics (linear through-thickness strain, rotations) of a Q1 solid core spanning several elements is the obvious locked direction. Remedies, each testable with the existing oracle before any learning: (i) collar depth 2–3 layers — mesh-scale content decays over ~1–2 elements, so the constraint-induced stiffening should fall roughly geometrically; (ii) a core with shell kinematics — Reissner–Mindlin on the mid-surface φ = 0 with nominal fields E t, D = E t³/12(1−ν²), κGt from t = 2τ/|∇φ|, joined to the collar by Kirchhoff kinematics u = u_mid + θ × (x − x_mid) — or an enriched solid core (Q2, EAS); (iii) a richer transition layer at the collar/core interface. Sizes: a shell core at mesh 1/16 has ≈ 600 elements and 4–5k dofs; the collar ≈ 1,800 cut cells and 30–50k dofs; exact condensation to the 12,798 trace dofs costs ~1e10 sparse flops plus one 12.8k dense front (~7e11 flops): 1–3 s per cell on the production node once cut-cell assembly is compiled (the present 17.7 s local assembly [REPRESENTATIONS TRIED] is tooling, not physics). Structure comes free: symmetry, PSD, exact rigid null space (strain-based elements annihilate rigid motions for any tensor), exact cube equivariance if the coarse mesh is symmetric, Loewner monotonicity in the fields, continuity in geometry (the discontinuous combinatorics — active set, trace set, ghost graph, collar cells — are computed exactly from the level set at inference), and the cancellation done exactly in FP64. Certification by construction: if the learned corrections lie within (1±δ) of the nominal fields, Ŝ lies within (1±δ) of the nominal model's S with no reference to the network; the remainder is the model floor, an oracle-computable, geometry-dependent number that must be brought under the gate by model design. Field labels are non-unique (the review noted several internal configurations give near-identical boundary responses); define per-seat oracle fields as the nearest-to-baseline optimum, which makes them unique and continuous in geometry. Deployment follows from the sizes: for a lattice, do not condense — assemble the reduced cell models (~50k dofs each) and solve iteratively; the fine trace is needed for certification and for mixed-fidelity assembly with teacher cells at load introduction. Storing dense S per cell (1.3 GB) was never a lattice option.

6.4 What this says about the network. Input: the whole sheet — global bending stiffness depends on the thickness everywhere — so a 3D field network on the active band (~23% of 65³ voxels ≈ 63k) with global receptive field, not six face images with receptive radius 0.23; V1's plateau at 27% on train and held-out alike [LEARNING ATTEMPTS] is what a local boundary model must give (and its banded-L + low-rank-M target had the cancellation problem on top). Output: smooth local fields on a fixed coarse structure (23k numbers in (e)), pretrained on the analytic baseline without the teacher, then fine-tuned on the whitened extreme-eigenvalue loss with the exact condensation in the loop (each Ŝ action is one sparse coarse solve). Rigid invariance, symmetry and PSD structural, not learned — the 38.8% diagonal-only attractor [LEARNING ATTEMPTS] is the signature of their absence. The local predictability of dof compliance (R² 0.98, leave-one-seat-out spread 16.8 [REPRESENTATIONS TRIED]; the repository's regression shows the node's material support fraction alone explains most of a 7.5e3 spread) is the empirical face of the same principle: local quantities are local functions of geometry; non-local ones must be assembled.

7. PRINCIPLES, COMPRESSED
1. S is a minimum-energy map; symmetry, PSD, the 6-dim null space and Loewner monotonicity in material, in GP and across active-set switches are exact.
2. The certificate is the two-sided Loewner sandwich; it is the only module statement that survives assembly, and it is tight.
3. The spectrum is a thin-plate spectrum: cond ≈ (L/2h_node) × 12(L/t)² ≈ 7e4; the floor and the 188 soft modes are shell bending; no stabilisation changes them.
4. Soft stiffness is a 1e3–1e4 near/far cancellation; bandwidth is not a lever; per-entry precision on a factor must be ~eps/√cond ≈ 1e-4.
5. The far field is Saint-Venant (6 resultants + few), low rank; the near field is a differential operator with cut-cell detail, full rank, Frobenius-dominant, energy-metric-irrelevant.
6. Membrane ∝ t, bending ∝ t³: the thickness-exponent test classifies directions physically.
7. With a hard active set the label is piecewise-analytic with monotone jumps every ~1e-4 in τ, O(1) only on stabilisation-dominated directions; the 59.8% event is stabilisation switching, not thin-connection physics.
8. Fragment directions are held by neighbours and never load-bearing; the bending family is load-bearing at full weight; only mode shape separates them.
9. Amplification ladder: operator ×7e4, factor ×1e2, subdomain DtN ×3–45, multiplicative physical fields ×1 — learn local, condense exactly.
10. The 1.111 obstacle is kinematic (a constrained collar interface), not material; test collar depth and shell/enriched cores with the oracle before learning.
11. A physically justified label is consistent, monotone, C¹ in geometry, cube-equivariant, and free of γ-determined directions; a smooth AgFEM-type blend achieves it at ~9 h of regeneration.
